key_insight: Incorporating depth estimation into thermal 3D Gaussian Splatting yields faster, more accurate thermal novel-view synthesis by providing geometry-aware initialization and constraints that reduce fusion overhead and reconstruction errors.
problem_solved: Thermal novel-view reconstruction is hampered by weak texture, modality fusion complexity, and slow/unstable optimization; the paper addresses robustness and efficiency when using thermal data for 3D scene representation.
method: Estimate dense depth maps (from thermal or co-registered sensors) and use them to initialize and guide Gaussian splat parameters instead of purely data-driven optimization.
Introduce depth-aware constraints during splat optimization and rendering to improve geometric alignment and reduce artifacts in thermal novel-view synthesis.
Evaluate performance trade-offs, demonstrating faster convergence and improved visual/metric quality compared to baseline thermal-only or unfused approaches.
impact: Enables more reliable, real-time-capable 3D thermal reconstruction for robotics and autonomous systems, lowering the barrier to deploy multimodal neural rendering in safety-critical applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: depth estimation → depth-guided Gaussian initialization → depth-aware splat optimization → thermal novel-view output
Before/after comparison: thermal novel views from baseline vs. depth-augmented Gaussian Splatting (side-by-side)
Performance chart: convergence speed (time or iterations) and quality metrics (PSNR/LPIPS) showing improvements
3D visualization: Gaussian splat cloud colored by thermal intensity with overlaid depth heatmap
paper_title: Supercharging Thermal Gaussian Splatting with Depth Estimation
paper_authors: Manoj Biswanath, Chenxin Cai, Hannah Schieber, Daniel Roth, Benjamin Busam
